auswahl.loeschenText: The entries will go to the Recycle Bin, from where they can be restored.

meldungen.dateiNachgeholt: Saved in the app, but not yet to the file: {grund} – it will be saved later.

browser.wartet: A browser is waiting for the database.
browser.nichtGespeichert: Change from the browser not saved: {grund}

fehler.zweifasVerschluesselt: The 2FAS export is encrypted. Please export it without a password.
fehler.jsonUnbekannt: This JSON format is not recognised. Supported: Bitwarden, Proton, Aegis, 2FAS, andOTP.
fehler.xmlNichtLesbar: The XML file can’t be read.
fehler.keineKeepassXml: This is not a KeePass XML file.

fehler.csvLeer: The CSV file contains no entries.

warnung.text2: After that, any program and anyone with access to that folder can read it, and syncing may take it along. Delete the copy when you no longer need it.

pdf.hinweis: If the embedded viewer shows nothing, download the file using the button at the top right.

fehler.keinCodeFoto: No QR code found in the photo.

hinweise.haeufig: Appears on lists of common passwords.
hinweise.einZeichen: Consists of a single repeated character.
hinweise.reihenfolge: Contains a keyboard or alphabetical sequence.

eintrag.text: Enter name, username and password yourself

dateien.text: Keep documents encrypted in the database

import.text: Bring in passwords and 2FA codes from other apps

kamera.text: Set up TOTP or read a bulk export

scan.fido: This is a sign-in code for passkeys, not transferable credentials. Passkeys are created by the system dialogue of the website.

totp.keinSecret: The code contains no TOTP secret.

neu.text: Creates a separate entry for it

bestehend.text: Attach it to an existing entry
bestehend.alleBelegt: All entries already have a TOTP

sammel.text: The code contains {n} accounts. Each one is created as a separate entry.

import.leer: No entries yet — assign at least password, username, address or 2FA key to a column below.
import.zusammenfassung: {n} entries — {pw} with a password, {totp} with a 2FA code. They will go into the folder {ordner}.
import.zusammenfassungDoppelt: {n} entries — {pw} with a password, {totp} with a 2FA code, {doppelt} already exist and were skipped. They will go into the folder {ordner}.
import.klartext: The export file contains everything in plain text — it’s best to delete it afterwards.
import.fertig: {n} entries imported from {quelle}. It’s best to delete the export file now.

gilt.hier: The version from here currently applies.
gilt.datei: The version from the file currently applies.

titel.eins: An entry was changed on both sides
titel.mehrere: {n} entries were changed on both sides

konflikte.hinweis: Since the last sync, these entries were changed differently here and in the file. Choose for each field which value should apply, or take one version as a whole. Until you decide, the newer one applies.

entschieden.datei: Decided: the version from the file.

liste.leer: No versions yet — the first one is created the next time you open or save.
liste.hinweis: The most recent versions of the file, newest at the top. Under each one you can see what it changed — tap it for details and to undo the change.

stand.zuruecknehmenTitel: Restore the entry as it was before this version
stand.aeltesterHinweis: This is the oldest saved version — what it changed compared with the one before can no longer be determined.
stand.nichtsGeaendert: This version changed nothing in the entries.
stand.gegenueber: This is what this version changed compared with the one before.
stand.liegtDa: This is how the file currently is.
stand.ganzZurueckHinweis: “Revert fully to this version” sets all entries back to how they were then — what came afterwards remains in the versions.

passwort.hinweis: The saved password is held in the core. It is only fetched when you click the field or choose “Show” — and only written back if you actually change it.

passkey.beschreibung: Sign in without a password — the secret key is stored only in this database.
passkey.hinweis: You create a passkey directly with the service (“Create passkey”). A browser extension or Android then asks WKeePass, and it ends up in an entry automatically.

anhaenge.dateienHinweis: Drag files onto the window, choose them below or create a new one. They are then stored encrypted in the database.

qr.hinweis: Scan it with an authenticator app. The code contains the secret in plain text — don’t share it and don’t let anyone photograph it.

scan.rahmen: Hold the code within the frame
scan.keineDekodierung: QR decoding isn’t available. Paste the otpauth:// URI as text instead.
scan.browserOhneQr: This browser can’t read QR codes — in the desktop and app versions Rust handles that. Paste the otpauth:// URI here as text.

viewer.nameUngueltig: The name must not be empty or contain a slash.

meldungen.leak: Caution: this password appears {n}× in known leaks.
meldungen.schonAngehaengt: “{name}” is already attached to this entry.

meldungen.nameLeer: The name must not be empty.
meldungen.schraegstrich: Slashes aren’t allowed in folder names.

statistik.inactive: not used for a long time

rat.passwortSofort: Change your password immediately — it was stored in plain text or was easy to crack.
rat.passwort: Change your password — it was stored encrypted, but that doesn’t make it safe.
rat.mehrfach: You use the same password elsewhere — change it there too.
rat.telefon: Expect SMS and phone scams in the name of this service.
rat.anschrift: Your address or date of birth is known — be sceptical of requests “for confirmation”.
rat.konto: Check your bank statements and credit card for transactions that aren’t yours.
rat.keinPasswort: No password affected. The main thing here: read emails in the name of this service critically.

hilfe.frage: What does a match mean — and what should you do?
hilfe.einleitung: Your address was in data that was stolen from a service and published. That doesn’t mean anyone has been in your mailbox. The address can’t be taken back — and you don’t need to. What matters is what was exposed along with it; the advice below for each individual breach depends on that.
hilfe.schritt1: Change the password with the affected service — and everywhere else you use the same one.
hilfe.schritt2: Turn on two-factor authentication where possible. WKeePass can manage the codes too.
hilfe.schritt3: Expect phishing: attackers target leaked addresses, often in the name of exactly this service.
hilfe.schritt4: Delete accounts you no longer need with the service — a forgotten account is an open account.
hilfe.schritt5: Use alias addresses for new sign-ups if your email provider supports it. Then a breach only affects one of them.
hilfe.abschluss: Once you’ve done everything, tick off the address. The next check will report any new breaches.

inaktiv.vermerkt: Noted — the entry counts as in use again.

aufwand.easy: can be done directly on the site

inaktiv.titel: Not used for a long time
inaktiv.hinweis: You haven’t used these logins for over two years. If you no longer need one, first delete the account with the service and then the entry — a forgotten account with an old password is a popular target. If it’s still needed, “Still in use” is enough.
inaktiv.kontoLoeschenTitel: Opens the {dienst} page in your browser where you delete the account yourself (link from the JustDeleteMe list). Nothing is deleted here.
inaktiv.zurSeiteTitel: Opens {seite} in your browser. Nothing is deleted here.

kontoFrage.text: Have you deleted your account with {name}? Then the entry can go too.
kontoFrage.papierkorb: It goes to the database’s Recycle Bin in case you still need it.

benachrichtigung.titel: WKeePass: new findings in the security check

passwoerter.one: {n} password is newly found in a leak.
passwoerter.other: {n} passwords are newly found in a leak.

lecks.one: {n} new data breach affecting your email addresses.
lecks.other: {n} new data breaches affecting your email addresses.

darstellung.farbschemaHinweis: System follows the operating system setting
darstellung.akzentfarbeHinweis: Warning and danger colours stay unchanged so that alerts remain recognisable
darstellung.spracheHinweis: The interface is reloaded when you change this

datenbank.appMethoden: What the app offers at all: {link}
datenbank.name: Database name

browser.stufeNichts: Linked browsers fill in without asking.
browser.stufeLegitimieren: PIN, master password or fingerprint before filling in.
browser.stufeHinweis: What happens when a linked browser requests credentials: nothing, a button press, or proof with PIN, master password or fingerprint. Passkeys always require proof.
browser.fristHinweis: Anyone who has just confirmed or unlocked is left alone for this long — a sign-in with several fields would otherwise ask repeatedly. After that you’re asked again. Doesn’t apply to “Nothing”; for passkeys only proof counts, not a button press; locking ends the grace period immediately.
browser.beimStartHinweis: If the database is closed when the browser makes contact, the small window opens straight away — PIN, fingerprint or master password, and the extension has its data. Without this, you unlock via the extension’s menu when you need something.
browser.erweiterungHinweis: KeePassXC-Browser — WKeePass speaks the same protocol, so it doesn’t have its own.
browser.eingetragenHinweis: “Set up” places a file for each browser that points to WKeePass — without it, the browser isn’t allowed to start WKeePass.

eintraege.importierenHinweis: Passwords and 2FA codes from Bitwarden, 1Password, LastPass, browsers, Aegis, 2FAS …
eintraege.iconsLadenHinweis: Once, directly from the site itself, without an aggregator — ideally when signing in, while it’s reachable. After that the icon is stored in the database and is available offline and on all devices.
eintraege.iconsNeuHinweis: Replaces the saved ones with freshly loaded ones
eintraege.namenHinweis: On: if the name is only an address, the entry is automatically named after the service — for example “GitHub” instead of “https://github.com/login”. Names you chose yourself are kept.
eintraege.namenPruefenHinweis: “Check now” compares all entries that have an address and, after asking, also replaces names you chose yourself.
eintraege.iconsAbruf: Icons are being fetched again — they appear as soon as they’re ready.
eintraege.uebernehmenText: For {n} entries, the name will be replaced by the name of the service.
eintraege.uebernehmenBrowser: In the browser, the security policy of other sites blocks the request — the hostname is used instead.

pruefungen.leaksHinweis: Have I Been Pwned — only a hash prefix is sent, never the password
pruefungen.emailHinweis: Via XposedOrNot — the email addresses from your entries are sent to this service
pruefungen.benachrichtigenHinweis: When a check finds a new breach — including the automatic one
pruefungen.automatischHinweis: When opening the app, if the last check was a while ago
pruefungen.loeschlinksHinweis: Downloads the public JustDeleteMe list (justdeleteme.xyz) with links to the deletion pages of many services. Nobody learns which services you use; nothing is ever deleted automatically.

appEntsperren.einleitung: What this device offers for unlocking. Which of them a database may use is set per database: Database → Unlocking this database.
appEntsperren.biometrieGeraet: {geraet} — offered on opening, replaces PIN and master password
appEntsperren.pinSchluesselbund: Set — protected by PIN and keychain
appEntsperren.pinOhne: Set — without a keychain, everything depends on the PIN
appEntsperren.pinKeine: No PIN yet. Applies to all databases.

export.zuruecksetzenHinweis: Settings only — databases, PIN and browser links remain
export.zuruecksetzenText1: Appearance, unlocking, checks, browser and Android return to their default values.
export.zuruecksetzenText2: What stays: the database itself, the list of your databases with their own settings, the app PIN and the browser links.

android.passwortmanagerText: Fills in logins in apps and in the browser, and offers to save new ones.
android.passkeysText: Sign in without a password. Your passkeys are stored in your database, not with Google.
android.kameraText: Only for the QR scanner: set up two-factor codes without typing the setup secret.
android.stufeHinweis: What happens when you tap a login in the list: nothing, a button press, or proof with PIN, master password or biometrics.
android.fristHinweis: Anyone who has just confirmed or unlocked is left alone for this long — a form with a username and password would otherwise ask twice. Doesn’t apply to “Nothing”; locking ends the grace period immediately.
android.stufeNichts: Logins are filled in without asking.
android.stufeLegitimieren: PIN, master password or biometrics before filling in.

stufe.bestaetigenMeldung: A button press is enough — no proof needed.

androidStart.text: For WKeePass to be more than a vault and help you sign in, it needs permission from Android. None of this sends data anywhere — your passwords stay in your file.

verschluesselung.hinweisSchnell: Opens quickly, even on older devices
verschluesselung.hinweisStandard: A good compromise that works everywhere — recommended
verschluesselung.hinweisErhoeht: More memory, harder for graphics cards — on iPhone/iPad, filling in via the keyboard no longer works
verschluesselung.hinweisHoch: Even more memory — no filling in via the keyboard on iPhone/iPad
verschluesselung.hinweisStark: Best possible protection, noticeably longer to open — no filling in via the keyboard on iPhone/iPad

erklaerung.einleitung: A key is first derived from the master password — deliberately slowly, using Argon2. Every guess an attacker makes has to do this same work.
erklaerung.durchgaenge: How many times Argon2 runs over the memory. Twice as many take twice as long.
erklaerung.speicher: How much working memory each attempt uses (1 MiB ≈ 1 MB). This slows down attacks with graphics cards the most, because memory is scarce there.
erklaerung.faeden: How many processor cores work at the same time. This makes no difference to protection — it only makes opening faster on your device.
erklaerung.eigen: Other apps and older files bring their own values, such as 50 passes with only 1 MiB. The app then shows the closest level and leaves the values as they are until you apply a level.

verschluesselung.eigenHinweis: Custom setting, for example from another app — roughly at “{stufe}”. Applying a level replaces it.
verschluesselung.hinweis: How long deriving the key takes — for you once when opening, for an attacker with every guess
verschluesselung.geaendert: Encryption changed — the file was rewritten.

versionen.hinweis: The most recent versions of this file — on opening, after saving, after changes from another device and after every merge. You can restore individual items or everything from them.

browserStart.text: With a browser extension, WKeePass fills in logins on websites, offers to save new ones and signs you in with passkeys. Your passwords stay in your file — the browser asks WKeePass every time. All three steps are needed.
browserStart.schritt1Text: Required: a browser may only start programs that are registered with it. The button places a small file for each browser that points to WKeePass — nothing changes in the browser itself. If KeePassXC is installed, the extension will then talk to WKeePass instead of KeePassXC.
browserStart.keinBrowser: No browser found — after installing a browser, you can do this in Settings.
browserStart.schritt2Text: Required: the extension comes from KeePassXC and is free. WKeePass speaks the same protocol, so it doesn’t have its own. The button opens the page in your browser’s store.
browserStart.schritt3Text: Once per browser: restart the browser, click the extension’s icon and choose “Connect”. WKeePass then asks for a name for this browser — only after that are passwords filled in.

karte.hinweis: Click to copy, double-click to open the entry

kern.fehler: The core reports an error at “{befehl}”: {ursache}

formular.pinMitSchluesselbund: The key is created from your PIN and a random value in the system keychain. An attacker would need both: the PIN and your signed-in session.
formular.pinOhneSchluesselbund: No keychain is available on this device. Everything then depends on the PIN alone — choose one that is long enough.

dialog.masterPasswortFalls: Master password (if the PIN doesn’t match)
dialog.biometrieGeraetHinweis: Replaces the master password — the key is stored in the security chip
dialog.biometrieSchluesselbundHinweis: Your finger proves who you are; the key is stored in the keychain
dialog.biometrieSchluesselbundHinweisPin: Your finger proves who you are; the key is stored in the keychain — an app PIN will be set for this
dialog.pinKuenftig: Also open with PIN in future
dialog.pinKuenftigHinweis: An app PIN will be set next for this
dialog.eingabeFehlt: Please enter the PIN or master password.

appPinAbfrage.text: The app PIN is needed to enable this database.

biometrieFehlt.keinFinger: No fingerprint or face enrolled — set one up in Android settings.

willkommen.text: To make the app easier to use, a PIN and/or biometrics can be used to decrypt your data and to confirm when retrieving it. After setup, simplified decryption and confirmation can be set individually for each database.
willkommen.geraetHinweis: Replaces PIN and master password. The key is stored in this device’s security chip — a PIN is then only a fallback.
willkommen.pinFehlt: Please set a PIN — or “Continue without PIN”.
willkommen.geraetEinrichtung: {name} will be set up the first time you open.

trotzdemSperren.text: If you lock anyway, changes since the last save will be lost.

zugriffEntzogen.titel: No access to the file any more
zugriffEntzogen.text1: Android has withdrawn WKeePass’s access to this file. This happens when another program deleted and recreated it instead of overwriting it.
zugriffEntzogen.text2: The offline copy is open — saving isn’t possible this way. Choose the file again once, and access will be permanent again.

appPin.text1: This PIN applies to the whole program. For each database you then decide individually whether it may be opened with it.
appPin.text2: After five failed attempts the PIN is discarded. There is no recovery — you then continue with your master passwords.

freigabe.offenNoetig: The database must be open for this.
freigabe.mitPinHinweis: The master password is stored encrypted; the app PIN is then enough to open it.
freigabe.fingerabdruckHinweis: The fingerprint is not a key here, but proof that it is you — the protection comes from the keychain alone. That makes this route weaker than the PIN, as an attacker needs only one thing instead of two. On macOS and Windows the hardware enforces the check; on Linux this program does.
freigabe.pinBestaetigen: Enter the app PIN to confirm:
freigabe.ohnePin: This can’t be confirmed without a PIN.
freigabe.geraetHinweis: Replaces PIN and master password when opening. The master password is sealed with a key that this device’s security chip only releases after {name} has verified you — a copied file is useless without this device.
freigabe.windowsZweimal: When setting up for the first time, Windows may ask twice.
freigabe.rueckfall: Fallback in case {name} isn’t working right now.
freigabe.pinFreigabeOhnePin: PIN authorisation can’t be changed without a PIN.

pinEntfernen.text: The PIN and all authorisations are discarded. After that you open each database with its master password again.

pinAendern.text1: The enabled databases are kept — they are re-encrypted with the new PIN in the background. So you do not need to enter any master passwords again.
pinAendern.text2: If you’ve forgotten the current PIN, the only option is “Remove” — then all authorisations are gone and every database needs its master password again.
pinAendern.ungleich: The two new PINs don’t match.
pinAendern.geaendert: PIN changed. All authorisations remain valid.

anlegen.name: Database name
anlegen.hinweis: The master password is the main key. There is no recovery — if it’s lost, the entries are lost.
anlegen.passwortFehlt: It won’t work without a master password.

entsperren.laeuft: An unlock attempt is already in progress.
entsperren.offlineKopie: The file isn’t reachable at the moment — the offline copy from {datum} is open. Saving only works again once the file is available.
entsperren.nurLesen: {format} is read-only — changes can’t be saved.
entsperren.entschluesselt: Decrypting … this will take a moment.

sperren.gesperrt: Locked — the values were removed from memory.

online.text: WKeePass needs no account and no server of its own. Some convenience features do query third-party services, though — choose which of them you want.
online.symboleHinweis: Fetches a site’s icon directly from it (e.g. github.com). The site sees your IP address.
online.namenHinweis: If only an address is given as the name, the page title is retrieved — directly from the site.
online.leaksHinweis: Have I Been Pwned: only the first 5 characters of a hash are sent, never the password.
online.emailHinweis: XposedOrNot: the email addresses from your entries are sent to this service.
online.loeschlinksHinweis: Downloads the public JustDeleteMe list so that the security check can link to the service’s deletion page for accounts unused for a long time. The whole list is fetched — nobody learns which services you use.
online.spaeter: You can change everything later in the settings.

text.unlock: The database is locked. A browser is waiting for it.
text.logins: The browser would like to fill in a username and password.
text.totp: The browser would like to retrieve a one-time code.
text.create: A new entry is to be created.
text.update: The password is to be changed.
text.delete: An entry is to be moved to the Recycle Bin.
text.passkeyRegister: A passkey is to be created.
text.passkeyGet: A passkey is to be used to sign in.

anfrage.warnung: Caution: the form is sent to {ziel} — not to the site you are visiting.

fehler.keineDatenbank: No database is chosen. Please open one in the main window first.

einstellungen.notizNever: Linked browsers fill in without asking. From the next request on — this one still needs an answer.
einstellungen.notizConfirm: A button press is enough — Cancel or Allow, no proof needed.
einstellungen.notizIdentify: PIN, master password or fingerprint. How long you aren’t asked again afterwards is set in Settings.
